rules.name: Model missing description
rules.short_description: A model entry in schema YAML has an empty or missing description.
rules.long_description:
dbt shows model descriptions in its documentation. State what one row represents and how consumers should use the model.

This rule checks models that already have a schema entry. Missing entries are checked by the test pack. Gold-layer findings have medium severity; other findings have low severity. These priorities are local policy. Waive the rule for an internal pass-through model whose purpose and grain are clear from its name.

References
- [dbt resource descriptions](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-properties/description)
rules.remediation: Add a description to the model entry. State what one row represents, the intended use, and the refresh schedule. Record the actual schedule rather than copying an example.

examples.title: Model without description
examples.good:
models:
  - name: stg_customers
    description: |
      One row per customer. Refreshed daily.

rules.name: Column documentation below threshold
rules.short_description: Too few columns listed in the model YAML have descriptions.
rules.long_description:
Column descriptions explain details that a model description cannot, such as currency, units, and the meaning of a date. Shared descriptions can use a `docs` block through `doc()`.

This rule measures columns listed in YAML, not all columns in the database. It skips models with fewer than 3 listed columns. The `column_doc_coverage` default is 0.8. Both limits are local review heuristics, not dbt requirements. Waive the rule for generated columns whose meaning is already clear.

References
- [dbt resource descriptions](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-properties/description)
rules.remediation: Document ambiguous columns first, especially amounts, dates, flags, and codes. Reuse a `docs` block for definitions that several models share.

examples.title: Undocumented columns
examples.bad:
columns:
  - name: amount
  - name: order_date
  - name: status
examples.good:
columns:
  - name: amount
    description: Net order amount in USD.
  - name: order_date
    description: Date the order was placed.
  - name: status
    description: Current order status.

rules.name: Source or source table missing description
rules.short_description: A source or one of its tables has no description.
rules.long_description:
dbt supports descriptions for sources and source tables. Record where the data comes from and what each table contains.

This rule can report two findings for one source: a missing source description and a list of tables without descriptions. Waive it if another team maintains accessible documentation for these definitions.

References
- [dbt resource descriptions](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-properties/description)
rules.remediation: Describe the upstream system, its owner, and the expected load schedule. Describe the grain of each source table. Link to maintained upstream documentation when appropriate.

examples.title: Source without description
examples.bad:
sources:
  - name: raw
    tables:
      - name: orders
examples.good:
sources:
  - name: raw
    description: Orders landed hourly from the OLTP system.
    tables:
      - name: orders
        description: One row per order.

rules.name: Project-level persist_docs not found
rules.short_description: Model descriptions exist, but no enabled persist_docs setting was found under models in dbt_project.yml.
rules.long_description:
`persist_docs` can write model and column descriptions as database comments on supported adapters, including Snowflake. Tools that display database comments can then show the descriptions.

This rule checks only the `models:` section of `dbt_project.yml`. It does not prove that comments are missing: model SQL or properties YAML can also enable `persist_docs`. Review the effective configuration before changing it. Adapter support and column quoting can affect persistence.

References
- [dbt persist_docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/persist_docs)
rules.remediation: Enable relation and column persistence at the required scope if it is not already set elsewhere. Run dbt with a role that can write the comments. Check the resulting database metadata.

examples.title: No persist_docs
examples.good:
models:
  demo:
    +materialized: table
    +persist_docs:
      relation: true
      columns: true
